objective: Build a minimal React calculator with four arithmetic operations, a responsive basic interface, unit tests, and a successful production build.
assumptions: The calculator accepts two numeric operands and one selected operation, then calculates on form submission.
Use the existing project tooling when available; otherwise use React with Vite and Vitest.
Standard JavaScript number precision is sufficient; expression parsing, calculation history, and advanced functions are out of scope.
requirements: Support addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
For division by zero, display exactly "Cannot divide by zero".
Accept positive numbers, negative numbers, zero, and decimals.
Provide a basic responsive UI with labeled operand inputs, an operation selector, a Calculate button, and a result or error region.
Include automated unit tests for arithmetic logic and essential UI behavior.
architecture: src/calculator.js: pure calculate function accepting two finite numbers and an operation, returning either a numeric result or an error.
src/App.jsx: controlled operand and operation inputs, submission validation, and result or error rendering.
src/App.css: minimal responsive layout with bounded width, flexible controls, and visible focus states.
src/calculator.test.js: unit tests for arithmetic and exceptional outcomes.
src/App.test.jsx: component tests using React Testing Library and a DOM test environment.

package.json and existing configuration: retain compatible tooling or minimally configure Vite, Vitest, React Testing Library, and jsdom; expose test and build scripts. Adapt file extensions and paths to existing project conventions.
implementation_steps: Inspect the project instructions, package.json, source files, and test configuration. Reuse existing conventions and avoid unrelated changes.
If no React application exists, create the minimal Vite React entry point and application structure. Configure npm run test as a noninteractive test run and npm run build as the production build.

Implement the pure arithmetic function with explicit operation dispatch. Check a zero divisor before performing division and return the exact required error. Reject unsupported operations and non-finite results.

Implement a semantic calculator form with two numeric inputs using step="any", an operation selector defaulting to addition, and a submit button. Keep input values as strings so empty values remain distinguishable from zero.

On submission, reject empty or non-finite operands before calculation. Render either the result or a concise validation error, never both. Clear previous output when either operand or the selected operation changes.
Add minimal responsive styling: a centered container, full-width usable controls on small screens, no fixed minimum width that causes overflow, and an accessible live output region.
Write arithmetic and component tests covering required operations, exact division-by-zero wording, validation, and output transitions.
Run the unit suite and production build, resolve failures, and manually verify keyboard use and layout at mobile and desktop widths.
edge_cases: Dividing any number, including zero, by 0 or -0 must display exactly "Cannot divide by zero".
Blank operands must not be implicitly converted to zero.
Negative operands and decimal operands must calculate correctly.
A result of zero must remain visible rather than being hidden by a truthiness check.
Invalid or non-finite operands must produce a validation error without invoking arithmetic.
Overflow producing a non-finite result must display a concise error instead of Infinity or NaN.
JavaScript floating-point rounding artifacts are accepted; decimal arithmetic tests should use approximate comparisons.
Changing inputs after a result or error must remove stale output, and a subsequent valid calculation must succeed.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting 7 + 3 displays 10; 7 - 3 displays 4; 7 × 3 displays 21; and 7 ÷ 2 displays 3.5.
Division by zero displays exactly "Cannot divide by zero" in the output region, without a prefix or additional punctuation.
Negative numbers, decimals, and zero results are supported.
Submitting incomplete or invalid operands produces a visible validation error and no numeric result.
All inputs have accessible labels, controls are keyboard operable, and Enter submits the form.
At viewport widths of 320px, 768px, and 1280px, controls remain usable and the page has no horizontal overflow.
npm run test completes successfully and exits without watch mode.
npm run build exits successfully and generates the configured production output.
verification_plan: Use table-driven arithmetic unit tests for all four operations, including negative operands, decimals, and zero results.
Assert exact error equality for division by 0 and -0, including 0 divided by 0.
Test unsupported operation handling and non-finite arithmetic results.
Use component tests to submit each operation and verify the rendered output.
Test blank-input validation, exact division-by-zero text, clearing stale output after edits, and successful recovery from an error.
Verify accessible labels and keyboard submission through component tests.
Run npm run test and npm run build from the project root and confirm both exit with code zero.
Inspect the application at 320px, 768px, and 1280px widths and check keyboard navigation, focus visibility, wrapping, and horizontal overflow.
risks: Existing dependency versions or test tooling may require configuration adjustments; reuse compatible project tooling before adding dependencies.
JavaScript floating-point arithmetic can display rounding artifacts; arbitrary-precision arithmetic is outside scope.
Native numeric input validation varies by browser; retain application-level validation and manually verify basic input behavior.
